holidays.name: National Cheeseball Day
holidays.description: Roll out the party classic! Today is for celebrating the glorious, round, nut-crusted orb of cheese that has anchored appetizer tables for generations. Grab a cracker and dive in.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its founder is unclear, but it has become a fixture of April 17 calendars.
holidays.funFact: Cheese balls became a hit in American entertaining in the mid-20th century. They are often rolled in chopped nuts, herbs, or crushed crackers for a crunchy coating.

holidays.name: International Bat Appreciation Day
holidays.description: Time to give a round of applause to our upside-down, nocturnal neighbors. Bats pollinate plants, spread seeds, and eat huge numbers of insects. Today is for celebrating them.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is meant to counter bats' spooky reputation and highlight their role in nature.
holidays.funFact: Bats are the only mammals capable of true sustained flight. Bats make up about a fifth of all mammal species.

holidays.name: International Haiku Poetry Day
holidays.description: Pick up a pen and squeeze your thoughts into three tiny lines. Haiku is a Japanese form that traditionally follows a 5-7-5 syllable pattern. Today is a good day to try writing one about your lunch.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors the short Japanese poetry form that is loved around the world.
holidays.funFact: Haiku traditionally includes a seasonal reference called a kigo. A poem about cherry blossoms would signal spring.
